newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Democrats to look at pharmaceutical cuts.
newsitem.headline: Australia Democrats to look at pharmaceutical cuts.

text.p: The Australian Democrats minor party said on Wednesday it would continue to push for a full review of the pharmaceutical benefits scheme (PBS).

In its 1997/98 budget released on Tuesday, the Liberal-National coalition government announced it would cut the scheme by about A$696 million over the next four years, saying the rate of expenditure growth on the scheme was unsustainable.
Democrats health spokeswoman Meg Lees said the party was sympathetic to the intention of the cuts, but closer examination of the detail was needed.

"We have a long history of opposing 'reform' measures which impact upon disabled and chronically ill Australians and we have repeatedly said that significant long-term savings in the PBS can be found through other means," Lees said in a statement.
The Australian Opposition has also identified the proposed PBS changes for reform, saying it was an area that required the "closest possible scrutiny".

Between them, the Democrats, the opposition, the Greens minor party and either of the two independents can block legislation in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, Pharmaceutical group F.H Faulding and Co Ltd said earlier that the federal government's plans to tighten spending on the pharmaceutical benefits scheme was not expected to have a significant impact on the company's bottom line.

"I do not think it will have a significant effect at all," chief financial officer Peter Maloney told Reuters, saying the move was aimed at branded drug products while Faulding produced mostly generic equivalents.
